text:
Daniil But is 21 and still finding his place. The 12th overall pick in 2023 out of Yaroslavl played most of October, sat out a two-week stretch, and was called back up this week as Utah's injuries piled up. He has two goals and four points in 16 games, playing about 10 minutes a night.

The early numbers are fair. Two goals on 1.9 expected, and Utah takes 54% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, a bit below the team rate. His own shot quality has dipped from his short stint last season, but at these minutes the sample is small. Evolving-Hockey liked his defensive impact in 362 minutes last season, 90th percentile at taking chances away, and our model's closest comparisons, Sandis Vilmanis and Shane Wright, are both players whose teams give up little with them out there.

History is patient with players picked where he was: of the 107 forwards taken 7th to 17th since 2005 with four-plus seasons, 87 reached 200 NHL games. His last KHL season translated to about 31 points over 82 NHL games. Our talent range has him around 11 goals. Watch his minutes now that Guenther and Schmaltz are out.
